newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: MALAYSIA PETRONAS AIMS FOR REGIONAL PETROCHEM HUB.
newsitem.headline: MALAYSIA PETRONAS AIMS FOR REGIONAL PETROCHEM HUB.

text.p: Malaysia's national oil company Petroliam Nasional Bhd (Petronas) said on Monday it aims to create a regional petrochemical hub in the country after announcing joint ventures with two major oil giants.
On Friday, Petronas signed a $700 million petrochemical joint venture agreement with Germany's BASF to build and operate a plant in Malaysia's central state of Pahang.
Later that day, British Petroleum said it would build a $150 million acetic acid plant in the northern Malaysian town of Kertih.
"For example our BASF joint venture will begin to be the nucleus," said Hassan Marican, president and chief executive officer of Petronas.

"It will spawn more facilities, and will be only one such facility in the region. Until we have such facilities, we can not attract such players to the country," he told reporters after Petronas Gas Bhd's annual general meeting.
"The reason these facilities are being developed is to attract... investments from the major chemical players of the world," he added.
